The East German – Molossian War (German: Ostdeutsch-Molossischer Krieg) refers to the unofficial conflict drafted by an unofficial declaration of war made by the micronation the Republic of Molossia to East Germany in November 1983. The conflict is famously known to be still on-going as of March 2026.
Background
In June 1972, Cuban President Fidel Castro gifted Cayo Blanco del Sur during, a small island, during a state visit in East Berlin to East German general secretary Erich Honecker. The island was renamed to Ernst Thälmann Island after German politician Ernst Thälmann. In the same year, a statue of Thälmann was built, which was toppled in 1998.
Declaration of War
In November 1983, then Prime Minister Kevin Baugh of the Kingdom of Vuldstein drafted a declaration of war to the East German Government for preforming military drills with West Germany. Baugh was stationed in West Germany under the United States Military, where one of the drills by East German soldiers allegedly disturbed his sleep. He later declared war on East Germany unofficially.
Rediscovery of the declaration
In September 2008, the document for the declaration was rediscovered by officials under the Government of Molossia while examining through old files. President Baugh then stated that the nation has continued to engage in the war, where he claimed that East German sovereignty lived on Ernst Thälmann Island. After the Reunification of Germany in October 1991, it allegedly proved that the East German Government still existed on the island with no one to call for a peace treaty.
